sanskrit_verse: लिखितं लिखितेनैव साक्षिमत् साक्षिभिर् हरेत् । साक्षिभ्यो लिखितं श्रेयो लिखितेन तु साक्षिणः ॥
transliteration: likhitaṃ likhitenaiva sākṣimat sākṣibhir haret | sā�kṣibhyo likhitaṃ śreyo likhitena tu sākṣiṇaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: A written document shall be validated by another written evidence; where witnesses are available, their testimony shall affirm the written record. Between witness testimony and a written document, the written record is superior; yet, witnesses authenticated by writing carry greater weight.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority of documented truth over oral assertion
executable_legal_axioms: IF a claim has written corroboration THEN prioritize over unverified oral testimony
IF witness statements contradict documented records THEN reject witness claims unless independently verified
IF written evidence lacks attestation THEN require conscious affirmation from capable witnesses
IF conflict arises in validation THEN favor documented proof aligned with dharma-sustained memory
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that documentary evidence holds primary authority. Witness accounts gain validity only when substantiated by or aligned with written records. The court must ensure no deviation from recorded facts occurs due to subjective interpretation or emotional influence.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality affirms that knowledge derived from accurate documentation precedes experiential recall. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential alignment between event, record, and recognition. Responsibility lies in preserving truth-integrity, not assigning blame. This aligns with non-punitive reality rule: error stems from misalignment, not malice.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Document authentication process through conscious witnessing
Reconstruction of disputed events using cross-referenced records
Realignment of participant awareness to factual continuity
Completion of incomplete testimonies through verified archival integration
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma prevails through documented truth, consciousness-aligned testimony, and restoration of factual harmony. There is no punishment—only realignment.
